title: Behaviour claims (verified documentation)
description: v0.1. A Muse Spark model writes a plain-English behaviour spec of a COBOL program as a list of CLAIMS; each claim is one sentence plus 1 to 3 concrete examples (input records as field values per the program's file layout, and the expected output field values). The verifier runs the ORIGINAL COBOL (GnuCOBOL, -std=ibm, in the sandbox when DIOCLE_SANDBOX_URL is set) on every example and decides: an example is `matched` when every stated expectation equals what the COBOL produced, `differed` when the COBOL produced something else (the actual value is kept), `unchecked` when the example was invalid for the layout, the program did not run, the program ended with a non-zero return code the example does not expect, or the expectation is weak (it compares only an output record count or a return code, never an output field value or stdout). Numbers are compared by value (+0.010 equals 0.01), not byte for byte; text ignores trailing spaces; stdoutContains is judged on the first 32 KB of stdout; at most the first 5 actual records are shown. A claim is `confirmed` when every one of its examples matched, which means the expectations the examples state held on GnuCOBOL: the claim's sentence itself is NOT machine-checked, only its examples are, `refuted` when at least one example differed, `unchecked` otherwise. The model never decides; GnuCOBOL does. Wording rule for every reader: 'confirmed on the examples tried', never 'proven'. A refuted claim is kept and shown: wrong documentation is caught, not hidden. Single-file programs only (the layouts come from sample.json); a multi-file program yields `skipped`. Also embedded as `behavior` in the run record (run.schema.json v0.13).

model.description: The model that wrote the claims (its output is a proposal, never evidence)

checkedWith.description: What decided: the original COBOL compiled with GnuCOBOL, for example 'GnuCOBOL -std=ibm'

examplesRun.description: Examples that actually ran on the COBOL

usage.description: Model calls made for this spec, token counts and estimated cost (null when a model in the calls has no known price)

skipped.description: Why no spec was written or checked (cap, unpriced model, multi-file program, model unreachable). When set, claims is empty.

fieldValues.description: Field name to plain value: a decimal such as '-36.50' for a numeric field, printable ASCII text for an alphanumeric one

statement.description: One sentence about observable behaviour in the output file or stdout

reason.description: Why the claim is unchecked, when no example could say

inputs.description: Input records in file order; each names every field of the input layout

expected.description: What the claim says the program writes. Only the stated fields are compared.

records.description: Output records by position; numbers compare by value, text with trailing spaces ignored

actual.description: What the COBOL produced; present when the example ran (absent when unchecked before running)

mismatches.description: Each stated expectation the COBOL did not meet, with the actual value (status differed)

reason.description: For unchecked: why the example was invalid for the layout, or that the program failed to run
